Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising. Attached are our initial redlines: we focused on export controls, subprocessor roles, and the SCCs section. A few things we'd like to confirm before we move to legal redlines:

Folks — brief legal take after reviewing Aisha's file: 

1) Delegation matrix: we should propose a two-column matrix (Redwood responsibilities / Pioneer responsibilities) attached as a separate exhibit. That will minimize ambiguity and map to the MSA clauses.

2) SCCs: preferable approach is to reference the latest EU Commission SCCs and add a short paragraph that any future SCC updates will be handled via an agreed amendment process. Avoid embedding the entire SCC language into the DPA.

3) Transfer-impact addendum: accept scoped addendum for the specific list of countries Pioneer provides. We must retain the right to require subprocessors' compliance evidence for any new data transfers.

4) Order Form backup residency: Redwood will propose the standard backup text Monica flagged. If Pioneer insists on a hard residency guarantee for backups, that's an order-level negotiation and may affect pricing.

I'll draft the delegation exhibit and a compact transfer-impact addendum for review. Monica / Laura — please advise if you want Legal to take the lead drafting or if Privacy should own the initial version.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
